A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RNA-FrameFlow with a matchable method, dataset, and experiment suite. All 24 pages of v2 and 26 pages of v4, including appendices, equations, tables, and figures, support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original RNA-generation experiments, quantitative comparisons, loss ablations, and analyses of structural realism and evaluation reliability.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds results on rotational and full-backbone self-consistency, atomic displacement, and ring puckering.

M1.justification: The frame atoms, eight predicted torsions, denoiser architecture, training losses, and sampling procedure remain unchanged. Replacing some uses of 'all-atom' with explicit backbone terminology clarifies the existing 13-atom output.

E1.justification: Both versions use RNAsolo for unconditional RNA backbone generation at lengths 40–150, including the retained augmentation using longer-chain crops. The new diagnostics analyze the existing data source and generated structures without introducing a new dataset or generation task.

E2.justification: Appendix C.5 adds an empirical comparison against RF2NA's P/OP1/OP2 frame choice using atomic B-factors in Table 9. This evaluates an alternative frame construction, not RF2NA generation performance. The MMDiff, Gaussian-noise, and RhoFold/Chai-1 comparisons were already present.

E3.justification: v4 adds rotational and 13-atom scRMSD measurements, puckering diagnostics, and B-factor analysis of 500 random RNAsolo samples. Figure 10 changes from valid-sample comparison to all 4,800 forward-folded candidates. The principal training budget, generation protocol, and validity threshold remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.4 tests frame orientation and full-backbone fidelity; C.5 examines the empirical stability of the chosen frame atoms; C.6 tests ring-puckering geometry. Together these substantially extend validation of the representation beyond v2's existing coarse self-consistency, local-angle, and clash analyses.

E5.justification: Figure 10 changes its stated summary statistic from the average among valid samples to the median across all samples. Existing timing over five runs and spread reporting remain; the PDFs do not establish an increase in training repetitions or seeds.

E6.justification: Tables 7–9 and Figure 17 add substantial structural results, including rotational/full-backbone scRMSD and atomic-displacement statistics. For length 120, the new median scRMSDs are 1.89 and 2.82, respectively. Figure 10 also reports a broader prediction distribution. Existing benchmark scores remain unchanged, including Table 1's 41.0% validity for RNA-FrameFlow and 0.0% for MMDiff.

T1.justification: Appendix C.6 introduces the five ribose-ring torsions through their atom quartets and defines the roles of pseudorotation phase P and amplitude τm for the new analysis. The flow-matching equations, losses, sampling mathematics, reconstruction derivation, and steric-clash definitions otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same contributions and headline claims: RNA backbone generation, 40–150-nucleotide coverage, over 40% validity, and data preparation to improve novelty. The introduction's backbone-specific wording remains consistent with the previously specified output.

C2.justification: v4 corrects puckering from rotation about a bond to nonplanar sugar-ring deformation and qualifies the frame atoms as having relatively lower displacement. Section 5 more explicitly connects implicit base-pairing and stacking to the model's omission of base atoms except N1/N9. Existing novelty and physical-validity limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B.3 explicitly documents 600 generated backbones, eight sequences each, and 4,800 forward-folded candidates. However, the sampling paragraph loses v2's numerical setting c = 10 and leaves 'c =' incomplete. Hardware, training hyperparameters, and code-access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds positioning relative to subsequent RiboGen and RNABPFlow work, including the connection to MultiFlow. New citations also support the puckering discussion. The established relationships to FrameFlow, MMDiff, RNAFlow, and inverse-folding methods are retained.

P1.justification: v4 makes focused terminology and paragraph revisions, adds appendix subsections and cross-references, and updates affiliations and publication information. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds Tables 7–9 and Figure 17, redraws and repositions Figure 10, moves Figure 2, and places several table captions below their tables. Publication headers and local layout adjustments are added, while most existing displays retain their design.

improvement.justification: The new atom-level self-consistency, frame-choice, and puckering analyses strengthen support for the unchanged method, while Figure 10 broadens the reported comparison beyond valid samples. Clearer backbone-specific limitations also improve precision. These are useful, limited gains; the main novelty and physical-validity limitations persist, and losing the c = 10 setting slightly weakens reproducibility.
